headline: High: Windsurf’s default filesystem, clipboard, MCP, and shell access can conflict with godot_rl_agents’ local workspace assumptions, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Windsurf can read workspace files, use MCP, and has clipboard access; if godot_rl_agents outputs are copied into that workspace or bridged through MCP, attacker-controlled content could be treated as instructions. The pair lacks any documented provenance or isolation mechanism, so the interaction is plausible but not proven by direct evidence.
conditions: IF godot_rl_agents output is pasted into Windsurf clipboard or workspace files
IF Windsurf MCP servers ingest content produced by godot_rl_agents without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the agents
Keep godot_rl_agents outputs in a separate directory
Require explicit human review before any MCP-fed content is acted on
Use a provenance tag or prefix on all transferred text
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and trust-boundary enforcement

B_data_leakage.rationale: Windsurf touches open files and workspace files and can egress broadly, while godot_rl_agents is open-source and documented only at repo level with no isolation guarantees. If sensitive code or secrets are present in the shared workspace, Windsurf may transmit them to its backend or model proxy. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default editor workflows.
conditions: IF sensitive files are opened in the shared workspace
IF Windsurf sends workspace contents to its model proxy or MCP-connected services
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared workspace
Open only non-sensitive files in Windsurf
Disable or restrict MCP servers for sensitive projects
Use a separate repo clone for godot_rl_agents
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data-loss controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Windsurf can write files, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses in a shared local filesystem; godot_rl_agents is a codebase that may also be edited in the same workspace. With no locking or coordination documented for either agent, concurrent writes can corrupt files or git history. The shared-filesystem pathway is explicit in Windsurf’s concurrency model.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same local repository or workspace
IF Windsurf auto-executes commands while godot_rl_agents files are being modified
mitigations: Run the agents in separate clones
Disable auto-execute in Windsurf
Pause one agent before the other writes
Commit or stash changes before switching agents
requires-engineering: add file-locking or orchestration coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Windsurf’s Cascade loop can act on generated code and commands, so if it consumes godot_rl_agents output as authoritative, mistakes can propagate into edits or shell actions. godot_rl_agents is a game-playing RL project, not a verified source of operational facts, so its outputs should not be treated as trusted instructions. The risk is real but bounded by human review and command approval defaults.
conditions: IF Windsurf uses godot_rl_agents output as direct input to code edits or shell commands
IF command approval is bypassed or auto-execute is enabled
mitigations: Require human review of generated actions
Keep auto-execute disabled
Separate factual outputs from executable commands
Add a verification step before commits
requires-engineering: implement output validation against source data

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention-sensitive data class is documented for godot_rl_agents, while Windsurf is a closed-source editor that handles source code and open files. Because the pair does not show a specific regulated-data mismatch, compliance risk is limited to ordinary code-handling policy gaps rather than a clear breach pathway. The other agent is not cited beyond its lack of sensitive data classes.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared workspace
IF organizational policy forbids closed-source tooling for that data class
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Windsurf
Use a policy-approved workspace for sensitive projects
Review retention settings in the editor
Restrict sharing of source files containing secrets
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
